base_note: The scratch source was archived from 9f08bbbb; d6bb9b50 changes only the plan, so the candidate applies on that later commit.
scope: Generic DWG entity name-resolution diagnostics for unresolved non-null layer and explicitly encoded non-null linetype handles, plus 64-bit truncation aliases. An ordinary tolerant reader still reports success and delivers its prior fallback names. Existing strict-complete and bounded-partial gates reject integrity errors and incomplete/dropped diagnostic ledgers. This diagnostic does not prove source handle role, mandatory-null semantics, immutable post-import identity, emitted-name closure, or general entity support.
authority: Open Design Specification v5.4.1 section 20.4.2, p.111, specifies entity common layer and conditional explicit linetype handle dependencies; generic parser hooks the existing shared name-resolution function after version-specific decoding. Relative handle normalization remains accepted when the resolved full value is representable.
change: After preserving existing lookup behavior, parseAttribs(DRW_Entity*) records EntityLayerReference or EntityLineTypeReference integrity errors when a non-null resolved handle is absent from its expected record-kind map, or its 64-bit value cannot be represented by the historical 32-bit map key. An linetype handle is checked only for ltFlags=3; implicit modes 0/1/2 remain untouched. Two enum values are appended without changing existing values or interface layout. Construction exceptions now increment the existing dropped-diagnostic ledger, preserving read softness while preventing strict completeness from treating lost errors as complete.

validation.focused: Normal 2/2 fixture-free CTests. The subtype matrix exercises 22 representative common entity families including BLOCK, ATTRIB, VERTEX and SEQEND through the shared resolver across AC1015/1018/1021/1024/1027/1032, implicit linetype modes, normalized relative handles, high-64-bit aliases with valid and zero low words, and missing/wrong-kind targets. A warning-filled integrity cap followed by a missing edge increments the dropped count; injected vector allocation and diagnostic-construction failures also increment it. The strict graph test injects a lost ledger entry and an entity error and requires destination sentinel preservation and same-adapter retry in ASCII and binary.
validation.physical: For the selected generated AC1027 one-layer LINE, source frame at decoded object-page offset 960 has body 66 bytes, handle-stream 40 bits, entity handle 0x36, original layer→0x12 and explicit linetype→0x10. Four inputs modify one target to missing 0x7e or a wrong-kind existing handle, and reseal object CRC and outer uncompressed page checksums. For each, `dwgRW::read` succeeds and calls addLine once with the legacy fallback; a kind-specific integrity Error records source entity and 64-bit target. The strict CLI refuses and preserves an existing sentinel. The unmodified input still converts strictly and produces byte-identical prior output. These are source mutations, distinct from in-memory diagnostic ledger tests.
validation.asan: Isolated AddressSanitizer build passes libdxfrw_dwg_entity_table_ref_diagnostic and libdxfrw_dwg_ac1027_default_graph_strict 2/2.

limitations: This does not reject null mandatory fields or role-4/valid-target tokens; both require separate source-profile qualification. The generic diagnostics do not authenticate mutable adapter state or inspect output and therefore do not claim whole-graph closure. The subtype test covers representative instances of the common resolver, not all possible dispatched DWG types or native consumers.
